question: A car travels 209 km in the first hour and 83 km in the second hour. What is the average speed (in km/hr) of the car for the whole journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the travel time for different segments of a journey is identical, the average speed is the direct arithmetic mean of the speeds.

Speed in the 1st hour = 209 km/hr

Speed in the 2nd hour = 83 km/hr

Average speed = (209 + 83) ÷ 2 = 292 ÷ 2 = 146 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 146 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered in the first hour (D₁) = 209 km

Distance covered in the second hour (D₂) = 83 km

Time taken for the first distance (T₁) = 1 hour

Time taken for the second distance (T₂) = 1 hour

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 
• 
 D₁ = 209 km 
 D₂ = 83 km T₁ = 1 hr T₂ = 1 hr Total Distance = 292 km | Total Time = 2 hrs 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 209 + 83

⇒ Total Distance = 292 km

⇒ Total Time = 1 + 1

⇒ Total Time = 2 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 292 ÷ 2

⇒ Average Speed = 146 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 146 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When a car covers two equal distances at varying speeds of x and y, the formula for average speed directly becomes 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a vehicle travels at different speeds S₁, S₂, ... Sₙ for strictly equal time intervals, the overall average speed is perfectly equal to their arithmetic mean: (S₁ + S₂ + ... + Sₙ) ÷ n.

Relative Speed

For two moving bodies, if they travel in the same direction, their relative speed is computed as the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If travelling in opposite directions, it is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).
